Chai-com Security Review

Execution trace of the multi-agent security pipeline auditing PR #8 in the chai-com repository. Findings are processed via AI correlation to filter noise and prioritize SRE remediations prior to merging.

Pull Request#8
Authorashok-yannam
Target Systemchai-com on Kubernetes
TriggerGitHub Workflow

Executive Summary

The chai-com workload exhibits a compounded risk profile within the multi-tenant cluster. Application-level vulnerabilities (DOM XSS, SSRF) act as direct stepping stones to critical cluster infrastructure due to a lack of network isolation and overly permissive cloud IAM roles. An unauthenticated external attacker can achieve full cloud account takeover in a single attack chain.

11 CRITICAL
7 HIGH
3 MEDIUM
6 LOW
21 INFO

Scope & Methodology

This threat model evaluates the chai-com service, its supporting Kubernetes platform, and the connected cloud account. The assessment follows a hybrid methodology combining STRIDE (threat classification), PASTA (attack simulation), and the MITRE ATT&CK for Containers framework (technique mapping). It is driven by a 26-agent static and dynamic scanning pipeline, with an AI correlation layer deduplicating findings and promoting chain-adjacent risks.

In Scope

  • chai-com application source (Node.js / Express + Angular SPA)
  • Helm chart and Kubernetes manifests for chai-com
  • Terraform modules provisioning the EKS cluster and node groups
  • Kubernetes cluster control plane (kube-apiserver, kubelet, etcd)
  • CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions) used to deploy chai-com
  • Cloud IAM roles attached to nodes, pods (IRSA), and CI
  • Runtime detection stack (Falco, audit logs, SIEM forwarders)
  • Data flows involving PII, PCI, and JWT secrets

Out of Scope

  • Third-party SaaS dependencies beyond identity & registry providers
  • Physical datacenter controls and underlying cloud provider hardware
  • Corporate endpoint (developer laptop) EDR coverage
  • Customer browser security beyond CSP enforcement
  • Social engineering and phishing vectors
  • Application business logic correctness (non-security bugs)

Assumptions & Dependencies

All analysis below rests on the following explicit assumptions. Breaking any assumption invalidates the corresponding findings and requires re-running the affected agent subsets.

Trusted Platform Primitives Assumption

The cloud provider's substrate (hypervisor, hardware, managed control-plane host) is trusted. Escape from the provider's trust boundary is out of scope.

Identity Provider Integrity Assumption

The external IdP used to mint JWTs is correctly configured and not itself compromised. Only JWT signing material held inside chai-com is in scope.

Container Registry Trust Dependency

The private container registry (GHCR) is assumed to be served over TLS with verified certificates. Supply-chain tampering outside the registry is covered by signature verification findings.

Network Reachability Assumption

Pod egress can reach 169.254.169.254 unless explicitly blocked. NetworkPolicy is enforced by a compatible CNI (Calico).

Agent Coverage Limitation

Findings are only as complete as each agent's ruleset. Business-logic flaws, race conditions, and cryptographic downgrade attacks may be underrepresented.

Environment Parity Assumption

The staging cluster used for Red Team replay is a faithful clone of production. Configuration drift between the two invalidates validation timing (2h47m).

01. Context Ingestion: Design & PRD Review

Context Ingestion & Design Review Agents
Missing Authentication Rotation
HIGH
Authentication relies on a single HS256 JWT without rotation, violating the "strong authentication" design standard.
Missing Namespace Trust Boundary
HIGH
No defined trust boundary between the workload namespace and kube-system. The design assumes single-tenant isolation but deploys to the shared multi-tenant cluster.

02. Code Analysis

SAST Agent
SQL Injection — Authentication Bypass
CRITICAL T1190
The application constructs SQL queries via string concatenation in routes/search.ts, allowing an attacker to bypass authentication and dump the database.
PoC: POST /rest/user/login {"email":"' OR 1=1--","password":"x"}
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
CRITICAL T1552.005
Unvalidated URL parameter in routes/profileImageUrl.ts allows internal network probing and access to the cloud metadata endpoint.
Secrets Detection Agent
Committed Cloud Credentials
CRITICAL T1552.001
A real, active AWS Access Key ID and Secret Access Key were found committed in the .env.example file.

Correlation & Validation: Code Scanning Reports

The AI engine merged the SAST SSRF finding, the committed AWS Key, and the jsonwebtoken CVE into a verified application-layer exploit chain.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation Steps

  • Revoke Keys: In the AWS IAM Console, revoke the compromised Access Key immediately and remove it from .env.example in the repository.
  • Fix SSRF: In routes/profileImageUrl.ts, implement an allowed domain list and explicitly block IP resolution to 169.254.169.254.

03. IaC & Pipeline

Terraform Agent
IMDSv1 Enabled on Node Group
CRITICAL T1552.005
EKS node group allows IMDSv1 queries without a session token (http_tokens = "optional"). This allows any pod SSRF to extract Node IAM credentials.
PoC: fetch('http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/')
Helm Agent
Privileged Container Escape
CRITICAL T1611
The deployment manifest runs the container with securityContext.privileged: true, runAsUser: 0, and hostPID: true.
PoC: nsenter --target 1 --mount --uts --ipc --net --pid -- bash

Correlation & Validation: Code + Infra Reports

The AI mapped the application-layer SSRF directly to the Terraform-provisioned IMDSv1 nodes, confirming an escalation path from the container to the Cloud IAM role.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation Steps

  • Patch Deployment Manifest: In helm/charts/chai-com/templates/deployment.yaml, update the container spec:
    securityContext:
      privileged: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  • Enforce IMDSv2: In terraform/eks-nodes.tf, update the node group launch template to set metadata_options { http_tokens = "required" }.

04. Cloud & Cluster Posture

Cloud Config & K8s Security Agents
Over-Permissive Node IAM Role
CRITICAL T1078.004
The IAM role attached to worker nodes possesses s3:* wildcard permissions, granting access to buckets outside the cluster's operational scope.
Unauthenticated Kubelet API
CRITICAL T1609
The Kubelet allows anonymous-auth on port 10250. Any network-adjacent resource can execute commands in pods without RBAC verification.
PoC: curl -X POST https://[NODE_IP]:10250/run/kube-system/tiller/c1 -d "cmd=id"

Correlation & Validation: Code, Infra & Cloud Posture

Connecting the overly permissive Node IAM role to the unauthenticated kubelet verified that node compromise equals total cloud data compromise. Detection coverage is 0%.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation Steps

  • Lock Kubelet: Edit /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml on all worker nodes to set authentication.anonymous.enabled: false and authorization.mode: Webhook.
  • Restrict IAM: In terraform/iam.tf, replace s3:* on the EKS Node Role with a scoped policy targeting only required bucket ARNs.

05 & 06. Defense, Network & Identity

Product Defense & Standards Agents
Missing Network Isolation
HIGH T1021
No default-deny NetworkPolicy exists in the namespace. East-west traffic is completely unrestricted across the multi-tenant cluster.
Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
HIGH T1059.007
No CSP header is emitted. This allows DOM XSS payloads to execute and exfiltrate session data seamlessly.

Correlation & Validation: All Prior Reports

Product defense weaknesses severely amplify the underlying infrastructure risks. The lack of NetworkPolicies combined with the lack of WAF/CSP means attackers face zero friction when traversing networks.

SRE Runbook: Immediate Remediation Steps

  • Isolate Network: Create k8s/network-policy.yaml with a DefaultDeny policy for the namespace, allowing inbound traffic only from the Ingress controller.
  • Add CSP Header: In server.ts (Express middleware), append Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'.

07. Validation & Attack Path Analysis

Threat Model and Attack Path Builder

The Red Team agent successfully utilized the findings generated by the pipeline to autonomously execute CHN-KILL-01 in the staging environment. Total time to cluster-admin was 2 hours and 47 minutes.

Primary Attack Path — CHN-KILL-01: XSS to S3 Exfiltration
Validation Status: FULLY_VALIDATED (Red Team, stage)
[INTERNET]
│
│ HTTP GET /#/search?q=<script> (no WAF)
▼
[ALB - ingress] <- Missing CSP (PRODUCT-02)
│
│ Reflected XSS payload execution
▼
[chai-com-app pod] <- SSRF in /profile (APP-01)
│
│-> fetch('http://169.254.169.254/...')
▼
[IMDSv1 - Node Metadata] <- No egress NetworkPolicy (NET-01)
│ IMDSv1 allowed (TF-01)
│-> RETURNS: AWS AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, Token
▼
[Cloud IAM - node-role] <- Over-permissive IAM (s3:*) (CLOUD-01)
│
│-> SELECT / DUMP -> 2.1M PII records from S3 bucket
│-> kube-system exec -> Cluster-admin privileges achieved
Red Team execution trace (2026-04-15): XSS achieved → Admin JWT stolen → SSRF directed to IMDS → Node IAM credentials extracted → S3 data buckets dumped → Cluster-admin pod exec achieved. Defensive telemetry generated 0 actionable alerts.

12. Remediation Roadmap

Sprint-bucketed action plan. Sprint 0 items break the validated kill-chain (CHN-KILL-01). Sprint 1 hardens detection and data protection. Sprint 2 shifts the service onto the paved path. "Continuous" items establish recurring safeguards.

Sprint 0 · Break the Kill-Chain ≤ 2 weeks

Goal: Collapse CHN-KILL-01 by closing any single required link
  • Drop privileged: true, set runAsUser: 1000, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false on the chai-com Deployment. (F-HELM-08)
  • Enforce IMDSv2 on every node group — http_tokens = "required" in terraform/eks-nodes.tf. (F-TF-06)
  • Apply DefaultDeny NetworkPolicy + explicit allow-list in the chai-com namespace, including egress block on 169.254.0.0/16. (F-HELM-09)
  • Disable kubelet anonymous-auth; set --authorization-mode=Webhook; close port 10255. (F-K8S-12)
  • Remove the default SA cluster-admin binding; create a scoped SA with minimal verbs. (F-K8S-13)
  • Revoke the committed AWS key, rotate to IRSA-issued short-lived credentials. (F-SEC-04)
  • Rotate JWT secret to RS256 (2048-bit) with short TTL and refresh tokens. (F-SEC-05)

Sprint 1 · Detection & Data Protection ≤ 4 weeks

Goal: Move MTTD from ∞ to < 15 minutes across the kill-chain
  • Enable etcd encryption-at-rest via a KMS provider. (F-K8S-14)
  • Deploy Falco with the falcosecurity/rules baseline + chai-com custom rules. (F-OBS-15)
  • Enable the K8s audit policy (Metadata+Request) and forward to SIEM. (F-OBS-15)
  • Add Ingress-level rate limits and enable OWASP CRS 3.3.x on the WAF. (F-DEF-19)
  • Implement CSP, SameSite=Strict cookies, Secure, HttpOnly flags. (F-DEF-19)
  • Replace the static kubeconfig with GitHub OIDC + short-lived cloud credentials. (F-CICD-17)
  • Rotate Grafana default admin credentials and integrate with SSO. (F-OBS-16)

Sprint 2 · Paved Path & Compliance ≤ 8 weeks

Goal: Move chai-com onto shared golden templates; restore compliance posture
  • Move SQLite off-pod to a managed encrypted database; tokenise PII/PCI fields. (F-HA-20, F-APP-01)
  • Adopt service mesh (Linkerd / Istio) for mTLS between services. (F-TLS)
  • Introduce Kyverno / OPA Gatekeeper enforcing Pod Security Admission restricted.
  • Require signed images (cosign verify) at admission; drop :latest tags. (F-IMG-10)
  • Implement JIT elevation for cluster-admin (Teleport / AWS SSO). (F-IAM-21)
  • Close PCI DSS and SOC 2 gaps; retest with DAST + Red Team agent. (compliance)

Continuous Always-On

Goal: Prevent regressions; keep threat model fresh
  • Re-run the full agent pipeline on every PR and on a weekly cron.
  • Correlation agent posts a single Slack digest per run to #sec-chai-com.
  • Threat-model diff review whenever the PRD, Helm chart, or Terraform modules change.
  • Quarterly Red Team replay of all primary chains; retire chain IDs closed > 2 quarters.
  • Tabletop exercise once per half for SRE + SecOps on highest-residual chain.
